chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has Muslim children and non-Muslim children, he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are upon their inheritances.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided when a non-Muslim parent leaves behind both Muslim and non-Muslim children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'al-mirath li-man qabala al-din' (inheritance follows the religion) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that a non-Muslim parent's estate is divided among their children based on their individual faiths rather than being consolidated under the Muslim heirs. This ruling is derived from the general Quranic prohibition of Muslims inheriting from polytheists and vice versa, ensuring that the non-Muslim children retain their share of the estate despite the presence of Muslim siblings. The narration underscores the distinct legal status of 'Ahl al-Kitab' (People of the Book) in inheritance matters, distinguishing them from polytheists in certain contexts while maintaining the core rule of religious separation in asset distribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from someone else,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and for him are Muslim children, and non-Muslim children, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (Muslims) are above their (other non-Muslim) inheritors’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from more than one person who has narrated the following: “
About the case of a Jew and a Christian who dies and has Muslim children and non-Muslim children, he (the Imam) said, ’The laws of inheritance apply to them.’” (Only Muslims inherit).
